jobs.title: Senior Manager, FP&A and Investor Relations
jobs.description:
About Redwood Materials

Redwood Materials was founded in 2017 by JB Straubel, co-founder and former CTO of Tesla, on a simple but radical idea: the critical minerals powering the energy transition already exist. They just need to come back. Today Redwood is the largest lithium-ion battery recycler in North America — recovering, refining, and redeploying critical minerals from end-of-life batteries back into the supply chain. On the energy side, Redwood has deployed the largest second-life battery project in the world, delivering power to AI data centers in months rather than years using proprietary energy architecture engineered entirely in-house. The company is profitable, the market it operates in is projected to grow 20 to 50 times over the next decade, and Redwood is the only company with the supply chain, the technology, and the operational scale to lead it.

Position Summary:

The Senior Manager, Financial Planning & Analysis is a high-visibility corporate finance role responsible for leading Redwood’s enterprise-wide planning, forecasting, and strategic financial analysis. This role partners directly with business unit leaders and the executive team to translate operational activity into financial insight, drive the annual operating plan and re-forecast cycles, and deliver decision-ready reporting to senior leadership and the board. The position is responsible for building and maintaining the consolidated corporate financial model and for developing the FP&A infrastructure needed to support a fast-growing, multi-site manufacturing company. This role is primarily performed in an office environment, with 3–4 days per week onsite at Redwood Material’s San Francisco location.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Planning & Forecasting

- Own Redwood’s annual operating plan (AOP) process, coordinating inputs across business units, manufacturing operations, and G&A functions to produce a unified, board-ready financial plan

- Lead quarterly and monthly re-forecast cycles, maintaining rolling views of revenue, cost, headcount, and capex against plan

- Build and maintain the consolidated corporate model, including P&L, balance sheet, cash flow, and key operating metrics

- Develop and improve long-range financial plans in support of fundraising, board reporting, and strategic planning processes

Business Partnership & Analysis

- Serve as the primary finance business partner to 2–3 business units or functional leaders, translating operational activity into financial insight and actionable recommendations

- Design and deliver monthly business reviews with clear variance analysis, bridging actuals to plan and forecast with crisp narratives for executive audiences

- Build financial frameworks to evaluate strategic initiatives, investment decisions, headcount plans, and resource allocation trade-offs

- Partner with Accounting to ensure a clean close process and accurate management reporting; help define what “good” looks like as reporting infrastructure matures

Reporting & Infrastructure

- Own and continuously improve the management reporting package distributed to senior leadership and the board, ensuring it is accurate, insightful, and decision-ready

- Identify opportunities to automate and scale FP&A processes; drive adoption of planning tools and best practices across the Finance team

- Develop KPI frameworks that connect financial outcomes to operational drivers, helping the business manage to leading indicators rather than lagging results

- Support ad hoc financial analyses and special projects as directed by the CFO and VP Finance

Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities

- 6-8+ years of total experience, with a track record of increasing responsibility in financial planning and analysis, corporate finance, or a closely related function

- At least 2 years of foundational experience in investment banking, management consulting, or a similarly rigorous analytical training ground

- Strong corporate FP&A experience in a complex, multi-site operating company; experience at a high-growth technology, industrials, or energy company is a plus

- Exceptional financial modeling skills—able to build and maintain complex, integrated three-statement models and executive-facing reports from scratch

- Demonstrated ability to communicate financial insights clearly to non-finance audiences, including executives and business unit leaders

- Experience owning an end-to-end planning cycle (AOP, re-forecast, LRP) in an environment with meaningful operational complexity

- Comfort navigating ambiguity and building process in a fast-moving, resource-constrained environment

- Ability to be onsite 3–4 days per week in assigned office(s)

In accordance with California pay transparency laws, the salary range for this position is listed below. Actual compensation may vary based on a variety of factors, including experience, education, and skills.

California Pay Range:
$190,000 — $252,500 USD

The position is full-time. Compensation will be commensurate with experience.

jobs.description:
About Redwood Materials

Redwood Materials was founded in 2017 by JB Straubel, co-founder and former CTO of Tesla, on a simple but radical idea: the critical minerals powering the energy transition already exist. They just need to come back. Today Redwood is the largest lithium-ion battery recycler in North America — recovering, refining, and redeploying critical minerals from end-of-life batteries back into the supply chain. On the energy side, Redwood has deployed the largest second-life battery project in the world, delivering power to AI data centers in months rather than years using proprietary energy architecture engineered entirely in-house. The company is profitable, the market it operates in is projected to grow 20 to 50 times over the next decade, and Redwood is the only company with the supply chain, the technology, and the operational scale to lead it.

Senior Operations Program Manager

This position will be second-in-command to the Senior Production Manager. This person runs the programs that keep operations moving: procurement, projects, continuous improvement, training, and the day-to-day administrative work. They step in for the Senior Production Manager when they're out. They lead from the floor, not the office, and are the link between operations leadership and the supervisors and leads running each shift.

Responsibilities will include:

Procurement & Materials

- Manage procurement for operations: spares, consumables, services, and capital items.

- Own the requisition-to-PO process from end to end. Keep cost centers accurate and spend on budget.

- Build and hold vendor relationships to delivery, quality, and cost commitments.

Operations Projects

- Lead operations improvement and capital projects from scope through commissioning.

- Coordinate cross-functional work across maintenance, engineering, EHS, and production.

- Track scope, schedule, and budget. Keep stakeholders informed and decisions moving.

Continuous Improvement

- Run the CI program for operations. Find the losses, prioritize them, and drive fixes to closure.

- Facilitate root-cause investigations and standardize what works across shifts and lines.

- Build and maintain the metrics and reviews that make performance visible.

Training & Development

- Own the operator training and qualification program.

- Build training content and competency standards with supervisors and SMEs.

- Onboard new hires and close skill gaps as the operation scales.

Administration & Operational Support

- Carry the administrative load that keeps operations running: reporting, documentation, scheduling, and records.

- Prepare data and materials for production meetings and leadership reviews.

- Keep procedures, standards, and records current and audit-ready.

Leadership & Coaching

- Act as 2IC for the Senior Production Manager. Carry the load and make the calls in their absence.

- Coach and develop supervisors and shift leads on people leadership and problem-solving.

- Serve as the liaison between operations leadership and the front line, carrying context both directions.

- Lead from the front. Be on the floor, visible, and hands-on when it counts.

Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities:

Required

- Working knowledge of standard operations and processes. You understand how the plant runs today and where it breaks.

- Demonstrated experience leading and coaching in an operational environment.

- Track record of getting things done across shifts and functions without needing to be told twice.

- Strong organizational and communication skills. Can own the admin without losing the plot.

- Willing and able to work onsite and be present across shifts.

Preferred

- Experience running projects, procurement, or continuous improvement work.

- Formal CI training such as Lean, Six Sigma, or equivalent.

The position is full-time. Compensation will be commensurate with experience.

jobs.title: Business Development Manager, Consumer Technology
jobs.description:
About Redwood Materials

Redwood Materials was founded in 2017 by JB Straubel, co-founder and former CTO of Tesla, on a simple but radical idea: the critical minerals powering the energy transition already exist. They just need to come back. Today Redwood is the largest lithium-ion battery recycler in North America — recovering, refining, and redeploying critical minerals from end-of-life batteries back into the supply chain. On the energy side, Redwood has deployed the largest second-life battery project in the world, delivering power to AI data centers in months rather than years using proprietary energy architecture engineered entirely in-house. The company is profitable, the market it operates in is projected to grow 20 to 50 times over the next decade, and Redwood is the only company with the supply chain, the technology, and the operational scale to lead it.

Business Development Manager – Consumer Technology

We are seeking a Business Development Manager – Consumer Technology, to join the team at Redwood. In this position, you will be responsible for managing relationships with consumer technology and device companies and establishing partnerships to source and recycle lithium-ion batteries. This role is vital to our overall mission and is a key driving force to meeting our company goals in accelerating the production of local, sustainable battery materials and ensuring that end-of-life batteries and materials are collected and processed safely. This position will include strategic account planning, account development, relationship management, and sales management across consumer technology partnerships. You will also serve as the commercial point person for Redwood’s Battery Bin program, a consumer-facing collection initiative that places battery drop-off bins at high-traffic community locations. You’ll work with business and technical teams across Redwood, collaborating to solve business problems with multiple stakeholders. The person who takes on this challenge, if successful, will be instrumental in paving the way for how this industry is shaped and the future of sourcing at Redwood.

Responsibilities will include:

- Build, foster and maintain relationships with consumer technology companies and device manufacturers to coordinate multi-level partnerships for the collection and recycling of lithium-ion battery materials. Align multiple locations and global stakeholders when necessary.

- Serve as the primary point of contact for consumer technology partnership, managing end-to-end account relationships from initial engagement through long-term partnership execution. Understand each partner’s product lifecycle, sustainability commitments, and battery disposal needs to position Redwood as their preferred recycling partner.

- Manage the product qualification process with customers, understanding the technical requirements for consumer device battery recycling, and communicate with key stakeholders internally and externally to manage qualification timelines and customers’ expectations.

- Accountable for making sure the business is on track – ensuring a strong mix of consumer technology partnerships, that we’re exceeding customer expectations, and that battery material is procured profitably considering sourcing cost, operating costs, and logistics cost to feed the machine that is producing the most sustainable battery materials in the world.

- Recognize customers’ product roadmaps and sustainability programs in detail, aligning our resources to the right programs and priorities, as well as identifying future growth opportunities in the consumer electronics battery sourcing space.

- Understand customers’ value chain and the influences of each player in the ecosystem. Direct global resources to manage the value chain appropriately as well as negotiate the various contracts (volume, prices, all other T&Cs) with customers.

- Own business development and operational oversight for Redwood’s Battery Bin program, including partner pipeline development, outreach, proposals, contracting, and expansion planning.

- Identify, prioritize, and develop relationships with Battery Bin host partners, including retailers, municipalities, universities, nonprofits, and public agencies. Evaluate deployment opportunities and lead the end-to-end launch process from partner qualification through go-live and ongoing account management.

- Develop partnership models and partner-facing materials for Battery Bin deployments, including grant-funded, leased, sponsored, or paid service structures, as well as pitch decks, implementation guides, FAQs, and related collateral.

- Track and report performance across consumer device partnerships and Battery Bin sites, using data to improve partner targeting, operational efficiency, cost-to-serve, and overall program economics.

- Coordinate cross-functionally with engineering, operations, logistics, legal, policy, communications, and compliance teams to ensure partnerships and collection programs are compliant, high impact, and operationally sustainable.

- Ability to travel 25% when necessary for meetings, tours, site visits, and program launches.

Desired Qualifications:

- Bachelor’s degree in business, marketing, sustainability, engineering or related fields. Technical background a plus.

- Sales/business/technical sales experience more than 10 years.

- Consumer electronics or lithium-ion battery industry experience is strongly preferred. Direct experience working with or at companies that manufacture, assemble, sell, or repair consumer devices.

- Deep understanding of consumer technology product lifecycles, sustainability initiatives, and circular economy programs within the consumer electronics industry.

- Experience building and scaling partner programs, channel programs, or distributed collection and deployment networks.

- Fluent in English for global communication to lead the account management.

- Strong leadership skills with logical communication.

- People skills to develop good relationships with customers even when in difficult to navigate situations.

- Data-driven mindset with experience tracking program KPIs and using performance data to inform strategy and improve operations.

- Smart, scrappy, entrepreneurial, science-loving, having a bias for action and a lot of grit.

- An ability to have fun while tackling hard problems!

- A passion for sustainability and making the world a better place!

The position is full-time. Compensation will be commensurate with experience.
